parsed.title: Discussion on tax filing, domain purchase, and app profitability

claims.text: P1 paid about 1000 UAH to correctly refile taxes after an inspector approved declarations without review for 1.5 years.
The main difficulty is correctly matching columns and numbers in the declaration, not the tax calculation itself.
The whole procedure takes about one hour with Excel, once per day, and a day per month for quarterly reports.
P2 said they haven't bought a domain yet.
P4 expressed doubt that anyone would buy a domain for the project.
P4 later described the project as a “free vibe‑code” experiment with little sense.
P1 researched earning on a personal project and found web platforms less profitable than Android/iOS.
P1 noted poor SEO, no external traffic, no ad revenue, and low user retention due to immediate paywall.
P1 observed a successful podcast described fast delivery (< 1 week) and a cross‑platform stack (Flutter) by copying popular apps.
P1 is skeptical that anyone would buy the product, betting it wouldn't sell for months.
P1 discovered the calculator works only with Ukrainian‑currency FOPs; they had to convert all transactions using the daily exchange rate.
P4 joked about not having paid 299 UAH for the app and hinted the password is stored in plain local storage.
P5 called it piracy and suggested writing to the author.
P1 believes most LinkedIn users could hack the app easily.
P4 described the app as a local‑first app with USD/UAH rates refreshed every 5 minutes, but the paid bundle contains hidden code.
